main_body: A red barn: a large tiled roof slope with a dormer (rows 6-57) above a plank wall with a big white-braced double door and two small windows (rows 58-90), on a grey stone base.
top_band: Red-orange scalloped roof tiles with a cream ridge highlight at rows 6-8, running down the slope to a cream eave edge at rows 56-57. Reads as a large lighter surface seen from above.
evidence: Down the middle column: the cream ridge cap is at rows 6-8. Below it comes the tile roof slope, which is many rows tall with per-tile highlights and a dormer. A cream front-edge line sits at rows 56-57, with a dark eave shadow at rows 58-60. Then comes the vertical plank wall with the door and windows in dark frames, and a stone base. The roof is a clearly visible top surface and the wall a distinct front face, matching how the reference building roofs read. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The roof is well textured, with 5 tones and scalloped per-tile highlights. The wall is thinner: vertical planks with only 2-3 reds, and large flat light-grey door braces and trim. The door panels and the dormer face are fairly flat. A heavy, uniform near-black outline runs around the whole building, roof, door and windows, which gives it a sticker look next to the reference. The reference uses material-toned dark edges selectively. Overall it is a little thinner and flatter than the reference.
